title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing customs that define the Beloit College experience, from ancient mounds to musical festivals.

cards.title: Spring Day
cards.subtitle: A Spontaneous Break from Classes
cards.notes: Celebrate the arrival of warm weather with a surprise day off. Students gather on Chapin Quad for music, food trucks, and the Holi Festival of Colors.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring tradition where classes are canceled for a day of outdoor festivities and community celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Spring Day is an enduring Beloit College tradition since the 1970s where classes are canceled to celebrate warmer April weather with outdoor picnics and music.
cards.source_title: Fridays with Fred - Spring Day - Beloit College
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in April; specific date is announced spontaneously by the college administration.

cards.title: The Turtle Mound
cards.subtitle: Sacred Ground and Unofficial Mascot
cards.notes: Visit the ancient effigy mound behind the Wright Museum. Out of respect for its sacred nature, students are encouraged to observe without walking on it.
cards.short_summary: A 1,000-year-old Native American effigy mound that serves as the inspiration for Beloit's unofficial turtle mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: The turtle-shaped effigy mound behind the Wright Museum of Art inspired the college's unofficial mascot and is a sacred space stewarded by the Ho-Chunk Nation.
cards.source_title: Mounds and the Museum • Logan Museum of Anthropology
cards.access_notes: Accessible year-round; visitors must remain off the mounds to preserve their structural and spiritual integrity.

cards.title: Folk 'n' Blues Festival
cards.subtitle: Beloit's Longest-Running Music Fest
cards.notes: Join the campus for a weekend of live music on Chapin Quad. This student-run festival has hosted legendary acts since its founding in 1972.
cards.short_summary: An annual music festival featuring a mix of folk, blues, and contemporary genres, organized by the student Programming Board.
cards.evidence_claim: The Folk 'n' Blues Festival is a tradition rooted in Beloit history, starting in 1972 when students invited Chicago-based artists to perform on Chapin Quad.
cards.source_title: Roots run deep at Folk 'n' Blues Festival - Beloit College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; open to students and the local community.

cards.title: The Senior Bench
cards.subtitle: A Gift from the Class of 1908
cards.notes: Look for the limestone bench near Eaton Chapel. Traditionally, only seniors are permitted to sit here, a privilege handed down at Spring Convocation.
cards.short_summary: A historic limestone bench that serves as a symbolic seat of honor reserved exclusively for the senior class.
cards.evidence_claim: The Senior Bench, a gift from the class of 1908, stands near Eaton Chapel and is traditionally reserved for seniors to sit on.
cards.source_title: Fridays with Fred: A photographic essay of the college in the teens
cards.access_notes: Located outdoors near the north side of Eaton Chapel; accessible to all for viewing.

cards.title: Blue Skies Award
cards.subtitle: Celebrating Good Cheer
cards.notes: Watch for the presentation of this whimsical award at Commencement. It honors a student who brings infectious positivity and humor to campus life.
cards.short_summary: A unique graduation honor given to a student who exemplifies good humor and improves the quality of life on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Warren Miller Blue Skies Award, established in 1982, recognizes a student for fostering good cheer and a good-humored perspective on campus.
cards.source_title: Blue Skies and Beyond • Beloit College Magazine
cards.access_notes: Awarded annually during the Commencement ceremony in May.

cards.title: International Gala
cards.subtitle: A Global Cultural Showcase
cards.notes: Experience a night of global fashion, music, and cuisine. This event highlights the diverse backgrounds of Beloit's international student body.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration of global cultures featuring student performances, a fashion show, and international food.
cards.evidence_claim: The International Gala is a campus-wide celebration honoring culture and global community through music, fashion, and international cuisine.
cards.access_notes: Typically held in November during International Education Week at the Powerhouse.

cards.title: New Student Days
cards.subtitle: The Buccaneer Welcome
cards.notes: Kick off your college journey with orientation activities designed to build community and introduce new students to campus traditions.
cards.short_summary: A multi-day orientation program for incoming students to connect with mentors and learn about Beloit's unique culture.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Days is where the Beloit College journey begins, allowing students to meet mentors and learn Buccaneer traditions before classes start.
cards.source_title: Fall Semester Checklist • New Buccaneers - Beloit College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in August for all incoming first-year and transfer students.

cards.title: The Round Table
cards.subtitle: Wisconsin's Oldest Student Newspaper
cards.notes: Pick up a copy of the student-run paper. Founded in 1853, it has documented campus life and student activism for over 170 years.
cards.short_summary: The historic student newspaper of Beloit College, known for its independent journalism and long-standing presence on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Round Table is the oldest student newspaper in Wisconsin, with its inaugural issue published in 1853.
cards.source_title: Print is Dying. - The Round Table
cards.access_notes: Available at various distribution points across campus during the academic year.

cards.title: Student Symposium
cards.subtitle: Showcasing Liberal Arts in Practice
cards.notes: Attend presentations where students share their research and internship experiences. It's a day dedicated to celebrating academic achievement.
cards.short_summary: An annual event where students present their independent research, creative projects, and field experiences to the community.
cards.evidence_claim: During the spring's Student Symposium, students share their research, internship, and study abroad experiences with the college community.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the spring semester; open to the public.

cards.title: Winterfest
cards.subtitle: Embracing the Wisconsin Winter
cards.notes: Enjoy the snow with activities like horse-drawn sleigh rides and ice skating. This event turns the campus into a winter wonderland for students.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal celebration featuring traditional winter activities and community-building events on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Winterfest is an annual event that celebrates winter with indoor and outdoor activities like horse-drawn sleigh rides and ice skating.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the winter months, typically December or February.
